# 1 Enoch Chapter 102 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QEn (Aramaic) | **Section:** Epistle of Enoch

---

**102:1** In-those-days-if-he-bring-a-grievous-fire-upon-you, whither-will-ye-flee, and-where-will-ye-find-deliverance? And-when-He-utters-His-voice-against-you, will-ye-not-be-affrighted-and-afraid?

**102:2** And-all-the-luminaries-shall-be-affrighted-with-great-fear, and-all-the-earth-shall-be-affrighted-and-tremble-and-be-alarmed.

**102:3** And-all-the-angels-shall-execute-their-commands-and-shall-seek-to-hide-themselves-from-the-presence-of-the-Great-Glory, and-the-children-of-earth-shall-tremble-and-quake; and-ye-sinners-shall-be-cursed-for-ever, and-ye-shall-have-no-peace.

**102:4** Fear-ye-not, ye-souls-of-the-righteous, and-be-hopeful-ye-who-have-died-in-righteousness.

**102:5** And-grieve-not-if-your-soul-into-Sheol-has-descended-in-grief, and-that-in-your-life-your-body-fared-not-according-to-your-goodness, but-wait-for-the-day-of-the-judgment-of-sinners-and-for-the-day-of-cursing-and-chastisement.

**102:6** And-yet-when-ye-die-the-sinners-speak-over-you: 'As-we-die, so-die-the-righteous, and-what-benefit-do-they-reap-for-their-deeds?

**102:7** Behold, even-as-we, so-do-they-die-in-grief-and-darkness, and-what-have-they-more-than-we? From-henceforth-we-are-equal. And-what-will-they-receive-and-what-will-they-see-for-ever? Behold, they-too-have-died, and-henceforth-for-ever-shall-they-see-no-light.'

**102:8** I-tell-you, ye-sinners, ye-are-content-to-eat-and-drink, and-rob-and-sin-and-strip-men-naked-and-acquire-wealth-and-see-good-days.

**102:9** Have-ye-seen-the-righteous-how-their-end-falls-out, that-no-manner-of-violence-is-found-in-them-till-their-death?

**102:10** Nevertheless-they-perished-and-became-as-though-they-had-not-been, and-their-spirits-descended-into-Sheol-in-tribulation.

**102:11** Now-I-swear-to-you, the-righteous, by-the-glory-of-the-Great-One-and-by-the-glory-of-His-kingdom, and-I-swear-to-you, I-know-this-mystery-and-have-read-the-heavenly-tablets, and-have-seen-the-holy-books, and-have-found-written-therein-and-inscribed-regarding-them.

---

*EMET notes: Ch. 102 contains the sinners' taunt against the dead righteous (vv. 6–7) — one of the most poignant passages in the Epistle. The taunt is essentially Epicurean: death equalizes, so virtue has no advantage. This is the exact problem the rest of the chapter and ch. 103 will answer. V. 11 introduces Enoch's counter-claim: he has read the heavenly tablets where the fate of the righteous is written differently. The 'mystery' he knows is the eschatological reversal.*
